what_this_is: The desktop apps use-an-app-here.mjs can work in on the person's own computer, each through the app's own tool server spoken to with the Model Context Protocol over standard input and output. A row is one server: `id` (what the tool's `app` input names), `label`, `about` (what it can do, in the person's words), `start` (the command that runs the server on this computer), `prepare` (run once when the server stops before it answers, as when it is not installed here yet), `env` (its server's settings: DAVINCI_RESOLVE_BRIDGE 1 keeps Resolve's server on the helper inside the open app, so it never starts Resolve itself), `needs_open` (the app program that must be running for an operation, as the ends of its paths in `processes`) and `opens` (how Trillion starts it when it is closed, with no one asked: `app` the name `open -a` takes, the row's label when absent; `ready` what must answer before the operation runs, such as `signed_health` with the `config` file of the app's loopback helper; `seconds` how long to wait, the file's `open_seconds` when absent): the app is launched in the background with `open -g -j -a`, without taking focus or showing a window, and if it does not come up the answer says so plainly, `places` (files the app itself runs, such as a script it loads when it opens: `file` beside this program, `into` one folder per platform as `{ platform, from, path }` where `from` names a base folder of the computer such as home, and `takes_effect` in the person's words), and how long it may take (`answer_seconds`, `prepare_seconds`; the file's own values when a row has none). `source` says where the server comes from and its licence. A `runtime` of `command` declares a server with no desktop app and requires its bounded local `check` to succeed before a native app job starts; an omitted runtime means `desktop` and keeps the installed-app row check. Whether a desktop app itself is on this computer, which version, and what that version allows are its row in computer/computer-sources.json. A new app is one row here.

apps.label: Filmcraft
apps.about: Cut, arrange and export videos in Filmcraft. Open files from the mounted Namespace in place and keep edits in one project.

apps.label: DaVinci Resolve
apps.about: Work in the project DaVinci Resolve has open: projects, media pool, timelines and their clips, markers, colour, Fusion, Fairlight audio and rendering. Works in every edition: DaVinci Resolve Studio through its External scripting (Preferences > System > General, set to Local), and the free edition through a small helper Resolve runs itself when it opens, which this tool puts in Resolve's scripts folder.

places.takes_effect: the next time DaVinci Resolve opens

apps.label: DaVinci Resolve project files
apps.about: Write and read DaVinci Resolve's own files without Resolve open: projects (.drp), timelines (.drt), grades (.drx), Fusion compositions, Fairlight audio plans, conform and deliverables, ready to import into any edition of Resolve, including the free one.

apps.label: REA reverse engineering
apps.about: Take an app or file apart on this computer and explain how it works: inspect, decompile and explain native Mac, Linux and Windows programs, .NET, Android, Electron and JavaScript apps, firmware and websites. Native decompiling uses Hopper, Ghidra or IDA where one is installed; looking at a website or an Electron app while it runs uses a Chrome-family browser.

apps.label: Local image models
apps.about: Generate and edit images from a visual brief on an Apple Silicon Mac. Inference stays on this computer; no cloud inference or Trillion-paid model. MFLUX and its MCP wrapper are MIT; choose a model whose weight license permits your use. First use downloads the chosen model.
